title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
description: Understand how Dynamic Programming identifies matching sequences efficiently using matrix-based comparison.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Comparing sequences is an important problem in computer science.

Applications such as version control systems, DNA analysis, and text comparison tools all require efficient sequence matching techniques.

The Longest Common Subsequence problem demonstrates how Dynamic Programming can solve these comparisons efficiently.

sections.title: Understanding the LCS Problem
sections.content:
A subsequence is a sequence that appears in the same relative order but not necessarily continuously.

The objective of the LCS problem is to find the longest subsequence shared between two sequences.

This requires systematic comparison between characters or elements.

sections.title: Why Exhaustive Search is Difficult
sections.content:
A brute force solution would examine many possible subsequences from both sequences.

As sequence length increases, the number of combinations grows extremely quickly.

This makes exhaustive comparison computationally expensive.

sections.title: Using a Dynamic Programming Matrix
sections.content:
Dynamic Programming solves the LCS problem using a matrix.

Each cell represents the longest matching subsequence length between partial sections of the two sequences.

The algorithm gradually fills the matrix until the final answer appears in the last cell.

sections.title: Character Comparison Logic
sections.content:
When two characters match, the algorithm extends the current subsequence length.

When characters differ, the algorithm compares neighboring values to determine the best partial solution.

This systematic comparison process efficiently constructs the final subsequence.

sections.title: Sequence Matching in Real Applications
sections.content:
LCS-style algorithms are used in plagiarism detection, file comparison systems, bioinformatics, and text editors.

Many collaborative software systems rely on efficient sequence matching to detect changes and synchronize data.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: The Longest Common Subsequence problem uses Dynamic Programming to compare sequences efficiently. Matrix-based computation eliminates redundant work and enables powerful matching systems used in many real-world applications.
